extracted.intended_audience: policymakers, colonial administrators, and educated readers interested in imperial/colonial governance and political theory
extracted.subtask_description: Normative and practical principles for administering dependencies and colonies: when to allow self-government, how to organize defence and representation, whom to appoint and how to train administrators, and how to avoid abuses from settlers or metropolitan interference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fullest measure of internal self-government for settler colonies
rubrics_metrics.description: Colonies of European race, equally with the parent country, possess the fullest measure of internal self-government. They have been allowed to make their own free representative constitutions by altering in any manner they thought fit the already very popular constitutions which we had given them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each colony is governed by its own legislature and executive, constituted on highly democratic principles; the crown/Parliamential veto is nominal and should be exercised (very rarely) only on questions concerning the empire, not solely the particular colony. Examples: colonies free to dispose of unappropriated lands; colonies free to tax imports from the mother country. This arrangement minimizes imperial interference in internal concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liberal distinction between imperial and colonial questions; limit imperial veto
rubrics_metrics.description: The veto of the crown and of Parliament, though nominally reserved, is only exercised (and that very rarely) on questions which concern the empire, and not solely the particular colony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A broad/lenient construction of 'imperial' questions should be used so as to leave internal affairs to colonies. The text gives the disposal of unappropriated lands as an instance of such liberal construction. Beware that inequality remains in foreign policy (colonies have no voice) and the mother country retains ultimate powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit colonial contribution to imperial wars to local defence unless voluntarily agreed
rubrics_metrics.description: In all wars, save those which... are incurred for the sake of the particular colony, the colonists should not (without their own voluntary request) be called on to contribute any thing to the expense except what may be required for the specific local defense of their ports, shores, and frontiers against invasion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the mother country may pursue policies that expose colonies to attack, it is just that she should undertake a considerable portion of the cost of their military defense even in time of peace; the whole of it so far as it depends upon a standing army.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mother country should bear a substantial share (or all) of standing military costs
rubrics_metrics.description: As the mother country claims the privilege, at her sole discretion, of taking measures or pursuing a policy which may expose [colonies] to attack, it is just that she should undertake a considerable portion of the cost of their military defense even in time of peace; the whole of it, so far as it depends upon a standing army.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial burden-sharing is part of justice to colonies that lack voice in foreign policy; paying for standing defences is especially incumbent on the imperial state.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open governmental service and dignities on perfectly equal terms to colonial inhabitants
rubrics_metrics.description: Open the service of government in all its departments, and in every part of the empire, on perfectly equal terms, to the inhabitants of the colonies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Channel Islands natives hold generals, admirals, peers, and prime ministers. Allowing leading colonial figures access to imperial offices satisfies legitimate ambitions, alleviates collective degradation, and reduces desires for separation (e.g., Ionian Islands' desire for union with Greece could be removed by such openings). Even if the number who benefit is small, their influence matters greatly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct rule of backward peoples may be legitimate if it facilitates transition to higher civilization
rubrics_metrics.description: There are others [dependencies] which have not attained that state [fit for representative government], and which, if held at all, must be governed by the dominant country, or by persons delegated for that purpose by it. This mode of government is as legitimate as any other, if it is the one which in the existing state of civilization of the subject people most facilitates their transition to a higher stage of improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In some societies a vigorous despotism may be the best mode for training people toward higher civilization; the ruling power should aim to supply a 'good despot' consistently. The ambition is to perform for subjects what a succession of enlightened absolute monarchs might do, qualified by superior foresight and humane motives rather than exploitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid governing a dependency by ministers responsible to a distant metropolitan public
rubrics_metrics.description: To govern a country under responsibility to the people of that country, and to govern one country under responsibility to the people of another, are two very different things... the last is despotism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ministers who are thinking of home (metropolitan) politics, who do not remain long in office, and who lack day-to-day local engagement are unlikely to govern well. Responsibility to a distant electorate promotes 'despotism' because the metropolitan public is not the proper judge of local needs; immediate agents of authority governed in the name of an absent master are at a disadvantage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Govern through a delegated, comparatively permanent intermediate body
rubrics_metrics.description: The only mode which has any chance of tolerable success is to govern through a delegated body of a comparatively permanent character, allowing only a right of inspection and a negative voice to the changeable administration of the state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such a body (e.g., the former East India Company council) is composed of persons with professional, place-specific knowledge, trained in the country, and having permanent interest in its prosperity. Advantages: no duty except to the governed, less subject to home-party jobbing, protects dependency interests before imperial tribunal, and produces continuity and expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select and train administrators via youth recruitment, competitive examination, and career progression
rubrics_metrics.description: Those by whom [a dependency] is administered be sent out in youth, as candidates only, to begin at the bottom of the ladder, and ascend higher or not, as, after a proper interval, they are proved qualified... competitive examination... unless by accident, there are no personal ties between the candidates for offices and those who have a voice in conferring them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The system must be calculated to form qualified officers rather than relying on chance. Competitive examinations recruit higher quality candidates and reduce patronage. Promotion should be merit-based; avoid opening higher posts to outsiders without the requisite local training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrict offices requiring specialized local knowledge to those trained in the service; except possibly the supreme post
rubrics_metrics.description: It is in no way unjust that public officers thus selected and trained should be exclusively eligible to offices which require specially Indian knowledge and experience. The only excepted appointment should be the highest one of all.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keeping appointments out of the reach of untrained outsiders prevents incessant lobbying and patronage. The Viceroy (or equivalent supreme governor) may be chosen from all Englishmen for general governing capacity, to avoid narrow service-class prejudices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use government education to proselytize; avoid appearance of coercion in religion
rubrics_metrics.description: The demand now so general in England for having the Bible taught, at the option of pupils or of their parents, in the government schools... To Asiatic eyes it is quite another thing... No Asiatic people ever believes that a government puts its paid officers and official machinery into motion unless it is bent upon an object... If government schools and schoolmasters taught Christianity... no amount of evidence would ever persuade the parents that improper means were not used to make their children Christians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Religious instruction by government schools—even 'optional'—is likely to be suspected as coercive and to undermine trust in government education. Proselytism risks compromising the utility and safety of government education and may threaten the stability of governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect natives from abuses by settlers and resist metropolitan pressure favoring settlers' interests
rubrics_metrics.description: English settlers... are of all others those who most need to be held under powerful restraint... Armed with the prestige and filled with the scornful overbearingness of the conquering nation... the simplest act of protection to the inhabitants against any act of power on their part which they may consider useful to their commercial objects they denounce... The settlers, not the natives, have the ear of the public at home.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Home public opinion and parliamentary access tend to amplify settlers' complaints; administrations must be prepared to resist such pressures to defend natives. The executive may find it politically easier to yield to settlers, but yielding undermines native protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize personal qualities and capacities of administrators; system must form such persons
rubrics_metrics.description: In a country like India, every thing depends on the personal qualities and capacities of the agents of government. The system must be calculated to form them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative quality depends on recruiting, training, and maintaining high averages among subordinates and top administrators. Allowing patronage or appointing unqualified persons results in decline; the 'monopoly' of the civil service is defended as a means to secure capable administrators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metropolitan responsibility chiefly useful for publicity and knowledgeable critique, not substitute for local governance structures
rubrics_metrics.description: The responsibility of the British rulers of India to the British nation is chiefly useful because, when any acts of the government are called in question, it insures publicity and discussion; the utility of which does not require that the public at large should comprehend the point at issue, provided there are any individuals among them who do.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publicity can provide scrutiny and allow a few informed voices to influence policy even if most of the public lack understanding; nonetheless, this is a limited benefit and does not obviate the need for delegated, expert administration on the spot.
